intervals.label: construction (MESA)
intervals.locator: arXiv:1802.04759 (Feb 2018): "MESA is under construction"; MESA page: "It is currently still under construction"; PRISMA+ news: electron source beam at its final location on 25 April 2024
intervals.note: February 2018 is the earliest source fetched that says MESA is under construction; the construction start is not stated. First beam from the MESA electron source at its final location in the LINAC tunnel on 25 April 2024; no source gives a date for first beam through the full machine.
intervals.quote: the new Mainz Energy Recovery Superconducting Accelerator (MESA) is under construction

name: MESA (Mainz Energy-recovering Superconducting Accelerator)
notes: 10 mA (6e16 electrons per second) is the design beam current quoted on the MESA page; it is not recorded as a spec because the A8 current dimension is only accepted in A and mA and the page ties it to the sample hit rate.

beam_energy.quote: where they are accelerated to up to 155 MeV, depending on the operating mode

summary.plain: MESA is a new electron accelerator being built at Mainz University that recovers most of the beam energy in superconducting cavities, giving a very intense electron beam of up to 155 MeV for precision experiments such as P2 and MAGIX.
summary.technical: Mainz Energy-recovering Superconducting Accelerator: electrons pre-accelerated to 5 MeV by the MAMBO linac enter an energy-recovery linac accelerating them to up to 155 MeV (external-beam mode for P2) with up to 10 mA (6e16 electrons per second); under construction within the PRISMA+ cluster; electron source first beam at the final location on 2024-04-25.
